about.title: About
paragraphs: The Intelligent Embedded Systems Lab (IES Lab Freiburg) pursues top-level research on basic and applied topics of wearable computing, digital health, machine learning, mobile health, biomedical engineering, and extended realities.
We integrate data to develop machine learning algorithms based on laboratory, wearable, and ambient data sources — for patient data interpretation and health knowledge extraction.

We develop embedded ML algorithms for very-low-resource sensor devices and investigate novel modelling and simulation methods for in-silico evaluation of wearable and implantable sensor and actuator systems.

alliance.name: Hahn-Schickard
alliance.description: Strategic research partner in microsystems technology, embedded AI, wearable systems, and digital health. The IES professorship was founded on Hahn-Schickard's initiative, bridging university research and applied innovation in Freiburg.

studentProjects.title: Human-Centered and Evidence-Aware Probabilistic Modeling for Causal Networks
description: The project focuses on expert-driven probabilistic modeling for causal networks in a clinical context.
The work extends a collaborative platform with LLM-based assistance for dynamic explanation of conditional probabilities.
The goal is to improve interpretability, traceability, and robustness of expert-based probability modeling.

studentProjects.title: Integration and Expert-Evaluation of LLM-RAG-Based Causal Network Modeling Pipelines
description: This project investigates the integration of large language models with RAG into causal network modeling workflows.
Students will build pipelines combining LLM capabilities with expert knowledge for interpretable causal models.

studentProjects.title: Cardio-compass: A wearable-driven mobile application for cardiovascular risk monitoring
description: This project develops a wearable-driven mobile application monitoring cardiovascular risk factors in real-time.
Integrates wearable sensor data with clinical risk models for actionable insights.

details.Requirements: Mobile dev (React Native / Flutter), wearable APIs

studentProjects.title: TinyML-based Real-time Human Activity Recognition on Ultra-low-power Wearables
description: Explores deploying optimized neural networks on microcontrollers for real-time activity recognition.
Focus on quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation for ultra-low-power MCUs.

details.Requirements: TensorFlow Lite Micro, C/C++, embedded systems

studentProjects.title: Real-time Body Tracking and Gesture Recognition for Extended Reality
description: Develops real-time body tracking and gesture recognition for immersive AR/VR applications.
Targets low-latency interaction for medical training and rehabilitation in XR environments.

researchAreas.title: IES Lab Tools
researchAreas.subtitle: Embedded AI, wearable devices, sensor systems, smart textiles
researchAreas.intro: Our lab provides a comprehensive ecosystem of hardware platforms, sensor systems, and software frameworks for research in wearable computing, embedded AI, and digital health.

tools.title: Wearable Sensor Systems
tools.description: Custom-designed wearable platforms for continuous physiological monitoring. Our sensor nodes integrate IMU, PPG, EDA, and temperature sensing in compact form factors.
tools.usage: Used across our digital health and biomarker research projects for real-world validation studies.

tools.title: Edge ML Development Kits
tools.description: Development platforms for deploying machine learning models on resource-constrained microcontrollers. We maintain toolchains for TinyML inference on Cortex-M and RISC-V targets.
tools.usage: Our custom firmware stack handles sensor fusion, on-device inference, and wireless data streaming.

tools.title: Biosignal Acquisition Systems
tools.description: Clinical and research-grade biosignal acquisition for ECG, EEG, EMG, and respiratory monitoring supporting wired and wireless ambulatory setups.
tools.usage: Integrated with our real-time analysis pipeline for automated biomarker extraction and event detection.

researchAreas.title: Digital Biomarkers
researchAreas.subtitle: Bio-acoustics, bio-systems modelling, medical AI, behavioral monitoring
researchAreas.intro: We develop novel digital biomarkers derived from wearable and ambient sensor data for continuous health monitoring, early disease detection, and personalized interventions.

tools.title: Acoustic Health Monitoring
tools.description: Bio-acoustic sensing systems for respiratory analysis, swallowing detection, and voice biomarker extraction using miniaturized microphone arrays.
tools.usage: Applied in our clinical studies for COPD monitoring and dysphagia screening.

tools.title: Behavioral Pattern Analysis
tools.description: Long-term behavioral monitoring using wearable IMUs and ambient sensors to detect changes in daily activity patterns indicative of health decline.
tools.usage: Deployed in longitudinal aging studies and mental health monitoring research.

researchAreas.title: Body Models
researchAreas.subtitle: Augmented/Virtual Reality, camera networks, projection mapping
researchAreas.intro: We investigate human body modelling using camera networks, depth sensors, and IMU fusion for applications in extended reality, ergonomics, and rehabilitation.

tools.title: Depth Camera Networks
tools.description: Multi-camera setups for real-time 3D body reconstruction and pose estimation using Azure Kinect and Intel RealSense arrays.
tools.usage: Used in our XR research for accurate full-body tracking without wearable markers.

tools.title: Projection Mapping Systems
tools.description: Spatial augmented reality systems projecting information directly onto the body surface for surgical guidance and physiotherapy feedback.
tools.usage: Applied in collaboration with the University Medical Center Freiburg.
